bugs.title: Messageboard spec is blocked on a file that no longer exists
bugs.body: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-05-messageboard-design.md carries `Status: design only. Blocked on the dispatcher (harness/dispatch.ts), which does not exist yet.` The dispatcher exists and is Gleam: harness/src/harness/dispatch.gleam. The dependency named in the status line was superseded, not satisfied, so a reader cannot tell whether the spec is still blocked. Posts are in fact half-built: dispatch.gleam logs them as events and routes nothing. Filed rather than fixed because docs/ needs asking.

bugs.title: Guard events do not say which worker was denied
bugs.body: guard.gleam:386 logs every decision as event/tool/decision and nothing else. Under `run --concurrency 3` all three guards write to one runs/<id>/events.jsonl, so a Deny cannot be attributed to a worker or a node. Rules already carries `holder`, the identity it locks under, so the guard knows; it just does not log it. Auto-filing bugs from guard denials depends on this, so it is a prerequisite rather than a nice-to-have.

bugs.title: A parked attempt leaves its proof file on disk, untracked
bugs.body: Rule30/Proofs/EvolveLeftSecondDiagonal.lean was left on disk when Vesper's attempt was parked, untracked and not imported by Rule30/Proofs.lean. Filed as a question rather than a defect, because the evidence cuts both ways: Rowan reports the re-dispatch built that same file unchanged and the verifier passed it, so leaving it saved a proof rather than losing one. What is genuinely wrong is that the file's existence carries no signal — nothing distinguishes `abandoned debris` from `a correct proof whose attempt was mislabelled`. Resolve this one by deciding, not by deleting: wontfix with a reason is a good outcome here.

bugs.title: hit_ceiling treats allowed_warning as a closed window
bugs.body:
Reported by Rowan, agents/Rowan.md 2026-09-06T02:05:00Z, filed by Keel.

worker.gleam:871 `hit_ceiling` saw a rate_limit_event at 0.94 utilization against the 0.9 ceiling and treated the window as closed. The event's API status was `allowed_warning` — a warning, not a refusal. Combined with an errored turn this parked a finished attempt as `rate_limited`, and a rate-limited attempt stops the run from starting more, so one misread warning can halt a whole run.

Rowan's ruling on the fix: only an api_retry carrying `rate_limit`, or a status that is not `allowed*`, means the window is actually closed.
bugs.resolution: hit_ceiling now decodes rate_limit_info.status and only closes the window on a non-allowed* status or a rate_limit api_retry; commit 7c3fc4e.

bugs.title: posts is required by the report schema but optional in the decoder
bugs.body:
Reported by Rowan, agents/Rowan.md 2026-09-06T02:05:00Z, filed by Keel.

brief.gleam:80 lists `posts` in the report schema's `required` array; worker.gleam:60 decodes it with `decode.optional_field("posts", [], ...)`. The two disagree, and the CLI's side wins: it rejects the structured-output tool call before the Gleam decoder ever sees it. A report with no posts is the common case, so this fires often.

Cost, observed: Vesper proved evolve_left_second_diagonal in one shot 85 seconds in, omitted `posts`, and the turn became an error. The `proved` claim the parking code adjudicates first was inside the rejected tool call, so it never counted, and the attempt was parked as rate_limited (see hit-ceiling-misreads-allowed-warning). The proof was correct and had to be re-dispatched to be recorded.

Fix: drop `posts` from the schema's `required` list, or make schema and decoder agree either way.

Keel's note: this generalises. Any field in `required` that a worker may reasonably omit is this same bug. The bug board's own `bugs` field must NOT be added to `required` for exactly this reason — an empty array is the common case there too.
bugs.resolution: posts dropped from the report schema's required array, agreeing with the decoder's existing default of []; commit 7c3fc4e.

bugs.title: Offline test fixtures point repo_root at the live checkout
bugs.body:
Reported by Keel and Rowan; root cause framing is Rowan's.

The offline run fixtures inject a fake verifier and a fake index writer so a test never touches Rule30/Proofs.lean, but cfg.repo_root is still the real checkout. So a test worker's proof file is written into the same Rule30/Proofs/ directory live provers write to: `gleam test` has been observed leaving Rule30/Proofs/HarnessProbe.lean behind.

This is the same defect as the incident in agents/Rowan.md where a test fixture with a colliding file name deleted a live proof. Two symptoms, one cause. Rowan's framing, which is the right one: offline fixtures should not point repo_root at the live checkout at all. Fixing that removes both.

Until then the only protection is the rule that tests must not run during a live run, which is unenforceable across two checkouts.

bugs.title: Guard tests bind fixed ports and a bind failure kills the whole runner
bugs.body:
Three independent sightings in one night: Rowan's first `gleam test` in a worktree died with a supervisor kill at the same minute another suite ran in the main checkout; a transient Eaddrinuse appeared during the Task 0 run from a just-exited process; and again during the Task 1 fix round.

The guard tests bind fixed ports, and mist's bind failure takes the whole test runner down rather than failing one test. So a stray `erl` from a previous run, or a second checkout running its suite, turns into a total and confusingly-attributed failure.

Two candidate fixes were discussed. Keel and Rowan both prefer picking ports from a free range at test time over a one-suite-at-a-time rule: the rule is unenforceable across two checkouts, which is exactly how it was hit. A bind failure should also fail its own test rather than the runner.

bugs.title: hit_ceiling ignores a refusal that arrives below the utilization ceiling
bugs.body:
Found by the Task 0 reviewer while checking the fix for hit-ceiling-misreads-allowed-warning.

hit_ceiling gates on `utilization >=. ceiling && !starts_with(status, "allowed")`. A rate_limit_event carrying a genuinely refusing status at, say, 0.5 utilization therefore returns False and the window is treated as open. This preserves the behaviour that existed before that fix and the conjunction was deliberate, so it is not a regression — but it is the opposite misread living in the same predicate: the fixed bug over-parked on a warning, this one under-parks on a refusal.

Filed rather than fixed because the reviewer's advice was a board line, not a code change in that task, and because nobody has yet seen a refusing status below the ceiling in the wild. Decide it with evidence: check whether the API ever sends one.

bugs.title: Line-ending churn reports untouched files as modified
bugs.body:
Seven files Rowan committed with LF show as modified in a Windows checkout the moment anything touches them, with `git diff --numstat` reporting zero changed lines. They are stat-dirty, not different.

The cost is not the churn itself, it is that it disguises real changes. Mid-plan this looked like another session had written into the checkout, which is a serious thing to see, and it took a numstat to rule out. Agents are told to stage explicit paths and read `git diff --cached` precisely so unrelated work is not swept into a commit; that discipline is much harder when seven unrelated files are permanently listed as modified.

The fix is a `.gitattributes` pinning `eol=lf`, which Rowan identified in its notebook and correctly flagged as Dib's call rather than an agent's. Do not commit the churned files as a workaround: they have no content diff, so staging them would bake CRLF line endings into the repository instead.

bugs.title: A wall node that becomes an open leaf aborts the whole run
bugs.body:
Reported by Rowan, after seeding the DAG's first `wall` node (evolve_left_diagonals_isEventuallyPeriodic) on 2026-09-06.

`schedule.next_to_start` has no `Wall` case: it ranks a wall node like any other open leaf once its deps are proved. `dispatch.start` then calls `config.model_for(Wall, _)`, whose ladder is empty by design, and returns Error("ladder exhausted for `X` although it is an open leaf"). `fill` propagates that Error, so the whole run aborts — not just that node — and it will abort again on every subsequent run, because nothing marks the node unselectable. The message's own wording ("although it is an open leaf") shows the author expected this to be unreachable.

The spec is clear that wall means "do not attempt without decomposing", so the fix belongs in the scheduler, not in dispatch: a wall node is not an open leaf, because an open leaf is a task the scheduler can actually start. Right fix is a `Wall` case in `next_to_start` that filters it out, with a test that a wall leaf is skipped and the run continues to the next candidate.

Not yet reachable in practice: the wall node's deps are three unproved nodes deep. It becomes live the moment that tier closes.

bugs.title: Long node ids run into the status column in `gleam run -- status`
bugs.body:
Reported by Rowan on 2026-09-06.

The status table pads the id column to a fixed width, and the new diagonal nodes are longer than it. The line reads

  evolve_left_fourth_diagonal_isEventuallyPeriodicopen      S     P1

with the id and the status fused. Cosmetic, and only in the human-facing table — the DAG itself is fine — but `status` is the command a human reads to decide what to dispatch, so it is the one place the board should stay legible. Pad to the longest id present rather than to a constant.
